\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{हालाँकि} (hālā̃ki)}{हालाँकि (hālā̃ki)}]{\hi{हालाँकि} (hālā̃ki) — although}

\label{lesson:HI-C371-halaki}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a political party, then the Hindi for to fix (a date).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हालाँकि}}
\textbf{\hi{हालाँकि}} — \emph{hālā̃ki} — \textquotedblleft{}although\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{हालाँकि} \hi{बारिश} \hi{हो} \hi{रही} \hi{थी}, \hi{फिर} \hi{भी} \hi{हम} \hi{बाज़ार} \hi{गए।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hālā̃ki bāriś ho rahī thī, phir bhī ham bāzār gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Although it was raining, we still went to the market.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{हालाँकि}} (\emph{hālā̃ki}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{hālānki}, \textquotedblleft{}although\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hālā̃ki}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hālā̃ki}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hālā̃ki bāriś ho rahī thī, phir bhī ham bāzār gae.} — Although it was raining, we still went to the market.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a political party, then the Hindi for to fix (a date), then say \emph{hālā̃ki} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{बावजूद} (bāvjūd)}{बावजूद (bāvjūd)}]{\hi{बावजूद} (bāvjūd) — despite (\hi{के} \hi{बावजूद})}

\label{lesson:HI-C371-bavjud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to fix (a date), then the Hindi for although.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बावजूद}}
\textbf{\hi{बावजूद}} — \emph{bāvjūd} — \textquotedblleft{}despite (\hi{के} \hi{बावजूद})\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bīmārī ke bāvjūd vah kām par āyā.}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{बावजूद}} (\emph{bāvjūd}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bāvujūd}, \textquotedblleft{}with the existence (of)\textquotedblright{}. Its second part is Arabic \emph{wujūd}, \textquotedblleft{}existence\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{अलावा} (alāvā)}{अलावा (alāvā)}]{\hi{अलावा} (alāvā) — besides, apart from (\hi{के} \hi{अलावा})}

\label{lesson:HI-C371-alava}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for despite, then the Hindi for instead of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{अलावा}}
\textbf{\hi{अलावा}} — \emph{alāvā} — \textquotedblleft{}besides, apart from (\hi{के} \hi{अलावा})\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{हिंदी} \hi{के} \hi{अलावा} \hi{मैं} \hi{अंग्रेज़ी} \hi{भी} \hi{बोलता} \hi{हूँ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hindī ke alāvā maiṁ angrezī bhī boltā hūṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{अलावा}} (\emph{alāvā}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ʿalāwa}, \textquotedblleft{}an addition\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{अड़ना} (aṛnā)}{अड़ना (aṛnā)}]{\hi{अड़ना} (aṛnā) — to dig one's heels in, to insist}

\label{lesson:HI-C371-arna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for instead of, then the Hindi for apart from.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{अड़ना}}
\textbf{\hi{अड़ना}} — \emph{aṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to dig one's heels in, to insist\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{baccā nae khilaune ke liye aṛ gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child dug his heels in over a new toy.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \hi{वह} \hi{अपनी} \hi{बात} \hi{पर} \hi{अड़} \hi{गया}, \emph{vah apnī bāt par aṛ gayā}.

\textbf{\hi{अड़ना}} (\emph{aṛnā}) is inherited from \emph{*aḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}stop\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 187).
